text:
Working with APIs is a common task for modern developers. An API allows different software systems to communicate by sending HTTP requests, such as GET or POST, to a server. In most cases, the server responds with data in JSON format, which is easy to read and use in your code.

Before making requests, you often need authentication, usually with an API key or token, to prove who you are. It’s also important to respect rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a given time. If you send too many, you may be blocked temporarily.

Finally, always handle errors gracefully. APIs can return error codes like 404, so your program should check responses and give clear messages instead of crashing.
